steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease an 8x4-inch loaf pan.
Combine sugar, butter, bananas, and eggs in a large mixing bowl. Add in flour, milk, vanilla, baking soda, and salt; beat well. Pour batter into the prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center of the loaf comes out clean, about 60 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Grandma's Homemade Banana Bread
raw_recipe.description: Grandma's banana bread recipe is a number one family favorite! It's been handed down from generation to generation. Get creative with add-ins.
raw_recipe.name: Grandma's Homemade Banana Bread

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease an 8x4-inch loaf pan.
Combine sugar, butter, bananas, and eggs in a large mixing bowl. Add in flour, milk, vanilla, baking soda, and salt; beat well. Pour batter into the prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center of the loaf comes out clean, about 60 minutes.

review.reviewBody: I followed this recipe to the letter adding only chopped walnuts. It was wonderful. Not too dry, not too moist - like Goldilocks' porridge - "just right". I made 2 loaves at once - one in a pyrex glass loaf pan and the other was a teflon coated pan. The glass pan did a much better job. Would recommend a glass loaf pan over a teflon one.

This is a sweet bread. It turned out moist and it's very filling. I added in 1 cup of chopped walnuts. I did not know what sour milk was, so I used buttermilk. The directions on this should have said to cream together the butter and sugar first before adding the other wet ingredients. As written, the butter did not blend in and left streaks and blobs, so I finally had to pull out my hand mixer on high to do the task before adding the dry ingredients. Other than that, everything is great with this. I would bake it a few minutes less the next time as it got too dark on top in a couple places and visually could be more appealing if it were more golden than brown on top.

I doubled up on the recipe and added 2 extra bananas. I also added in some chopped pecans. I made half of them as muffins and the remaining batter I baked in a loaf pan. In making the soured milk I used milk with a little lemon juice. These were moist and so delicious. I saw how some said they were dry but I did not experience this. Maybe they were baked too long perhaps. Will definitely make this again. Great way to use up over ripe bananas.

I just made this recipe when I couldn't find my favorite one from years ago. I used 5 good sized bananas, regular milk, a quarter cup of honey in place of 1/2 c of the sugar. I creamed the butter, sugar & honey together then the eggs. I combined the dry ingredients in a small bowl. I mashed the bananas in a separate bowl, added milk and vanilla to them, then alternately beat in the banana mixture and the dry ingredients into the butter mixture until it was all moist. 
I made 24 muffins, cooked at 350 on the convection bake setting, for only 25 minutes. I filled the muffin cups almost to the top. They came out perfect!

Excellent recipe and easy because you mix everything in at once. I added chopped macadamia nuts and white chips and my husband said it was the best banana bread he ever had. I made it last week and got more bananas and now I’m making it again. To make the sour milk I put half a teaspoon of white vinegar in the third cup measuring cup and filled it up the rest of the way with milk. I let that sit while getting the other ingredients ready. I also decreased the sugar to one and a third cups because the chips are very sweet. This recipe is a keeper.

I loved this recipe. I used 3 small frozen bananas - defrosted and mashed and for my chocoholic daughter I added 3/4 cup of chocolate chips. I didn't have the whole amount of butter, so I substituted 2 tbls of coconut oil. Other than that, I followed the recipe to the letter. It took about 15 minutes more to bake than the recipe - an hour and 15 minutes altogether. It came out beautifully - moist and delicious! I made it last night and it is almost gone! I will definitely make this again. Thank you!

Made this turned out delicious I didn't have sour milk so I used a 1/3 cup and I measured half milk and half vinegar and it still turned out amazing! Just start with the wet ingredients first and then put the flour last. I did not over mix it I just mixed until the flour was incorporated and I baked it in a 350 degree electric oven in a teflon pan for 60 mins.

If your not into a really sweet bread you might want to cut back on the sugar.

Great recipe. I tried other recipes before but it turned out dried. With this recipe, it came out great. I made the sour milk at home, instead of going to the store to get some. I just mixed 1 cup of milk with 1 table spoon of lemon juice, while I was mixing the rest of ingredients. It works perfectly. I reduced the sugar in half but I added an extra banana. I used brown sugar instead of white and I added walnuts for a perfect texture. Now I just need to enjoy it with vanilla ice cream and I’ll be done. ??

I doubled the recipe and got two 9 inch loafs, 12 mini muffins and 12 big muffins. I used 6oz of whipped cream cheese instead of sour milk. I also always add cinnamon, cloves and a little pumpkin pie seasoning to my banana bread for a little spice flavor. I used the remaining 2oz of cream cheese and 2 extra bananas mixed with cream cheese frosting to make the muffins more like cupcakes. They were a hit with the kids and my husband took the bread to work with some extra frosting.... they requested more!!! Great recipe!!

This is my all-time most used recipe as long as we don't count Mac-n-cheese. I make it with however many bananas we have turning brown. Turns out great every time. It is very tender & lends itself to thick slices. Things that help me:
1. grease & flour the pan
2. beat the sugar, butter, eggs & vanilla til fluffy before adding other ingredients
3. add 1/2 bag of chocolate chips (for obvious reasons)
4. bake til toothpick comes out clean
Enjoy & get your slice before the family snarfs it all down. :)

I love this banana bread recipe and make it often. I usually make this at 1.5 times the ingredients and it makes 2 loaves the perfect size, otherwise the single recipe is just a little too much batter for one pan. My husband prefers banana bread without nuts and I prefer it with so when I make the extra batter we can each have a loaf of our own, and I add nuts after I’ve poured half the batter in the first pan.
Followed recipe as written, but added a dash of orange juice and a half a cup of walnuts

Best banana bread I have ever made! My husband agreed. I made it exactly as written, except my loaf pan is stoneware, which takes longer to finish cooking. The flavor, texture, moisture level, everything...PERFECT. Surprisingly even better the next day at room temperature.
a general question: when baking mini loaves how much time to cut from the regular loaf time? this bread is delicious...followed the recipe to a tee...and I like it.

I made this recipe nearly as written, my only change was to use gluten free flour instead of all purpose. For the sour milked, I mixed a splash or two of apple cider vinegar with my milk and set aside for a few minutes. Lemon juice can also be used to make soured milk or you can use buttermilk instead. Due to the gluten free flour I did need to bake longer than 1 hour, but I expected that. The banana bread was a sweet banana bread that my husband loved. I can see myself making it again with the excess bananas I always have during cross country and track season.

I only had med. eggs, so substituted three for the (2) large and added walnuts. I decided to toss in an extra 1/4 c. flour due to the extra wet ingredient and ended up getting a yield of (5) mini-loaves. Yum.

The recipe was easy to follow. I found that it was very moist. The batter seemed a little bit heavy. I should have divided it into two loaves instead of one. The texture was also too moist for my taste. The bread had a great flavor.

The beauty of this recipe is that it can be made with a good outcome exactly as written. And, it can be used as a spring board to get something that you or your family like a bit better. Like cinnamon? Add cinnamon. Like nuts? Add nuts. Like it a bit less sweet? Add less sugar. Etc., etc., etc. I make mine with 3/4 cup of honey instead of the granulated sugar that's called for because I have a health conscious family member who avoids processed sugar. It does get darker in color, FYI.
